target_customer: Office workers via employers and food vendors at launch; later foodservice operators such as cafes and campuses
problem: Fresh smoothies are slow to make and clean up after; the company first delivered them and then built a pod-based self-cleaning blender.
business_model: Hardware placed free through vendors with revenue from single-serve pods ($3.50 to $5 per pod, per TechCrunch 2016)

founders.name: Elise Polezel
founders.background_notes: Later CEO of HigherMe (YC W15) per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: By 2016 the product was a self-cleaning pod blender needing hardware design, manufacturing and food safety, hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Pod ecosystem and hardware design could lock in vendors, but a single product with no stated patents or scale in the sources.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch 2016 compared it to Juicero, which had raised $70 million. No evidence in sources that an incumbent copied or bought it.

market_need_then: In 2014 chefs at Twitter, Dropbox and Stripe ordered its delivered smoothies for tech workers per TechCrunch, a signal of office demand. In 2016 pilots ran at SAP, Lucasfilm and Uber offices.

branding.domain_note: Current site getreplenish.com, a prefixed domain, suggesting replenish.com was unavailable; not stated by a source.

rebrands.why: Not stated; coincided with the move from delivery to smoothie machines.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the rename and product, but no community or merch evidence. The current site uses registered marks Replenish, Genesis, Hydroblend and Hydroclean.

pivots.from: Cold-pressed smoothie delivery to San Francisco offices (LivBlends)
pivots.why: Not stated; TechCrunch 2016 reports the shift from delivery to hardware.

pivots.from: Office pod machines via food vendors
pivots.why: Not stated; current website targets cafes, quick-service restaurants and campuses.

outcome_analysis: LivBlends began as a smoothie delivery service in YC S14, then moved to a pod-based self-cleaning blender, renamed itself Replenish and raised a $3.8 million seed in 2016. YC lists it as acquired but no acquirer, date or price was found, and the company's own website still operates under the Replenish brand in Delray Beach, Florida, so the outcome is unclear and may be a data error.
notes: YC status Acquired conflicts with the live company site and no acquisition source was found (only Seedtable lists an unnamed acquisition), so exit type is unknown. Investors Tandem Capital and Great Oaks come from Seedtable, TechCrunch gives only the amount. CB Insights shows about 6.9M over 7 rounds with inconsistent dates, unverified. No dated competitor for 2014 found; Juicero comparison dates to 2016 so it is not recorded as competition at founding.
